from.place: ## Proof, as a whole (degrees $q>2$): the blueprint proof concludes 'For total degree $q>2$ there are thus no differentials into or out of $H^q(C,\eta_*M)$. It equals $H^q(k(C),M)=0$'; the split replaces this generic-point assembly by the route of the Lean proof AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve.subsingleton_sheafH_of_three_le_of_forall (HighDegreeVanishing.lean), and this node is used in steps 4 and 5 (for $U$ and for the affine curves $V_a\times_CU$).

title: H^2 of a torsion sheaf on an affine curve vanishes
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $C$ an affine curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves] (an affine scheme, separated and of finite type over $k$, of dimension at most one; it may be empty, disconnected, singular or have zero-dimensional components). For every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $C_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], $H^2(C_{\Et},F)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].
